title: Self-Sycophancy: Do Models Defend Their Own Prior Wrong Answers More Than a Stranger's?

original_idea.body: Self-Sycophancy. Problem: the prevalence of a model defending its own prior wrong answer (self-consistency bias) vs ordinary user-sycophancy is unknown. Direction: compare 'you previously answered X' vs 'another model answered X' then push back, measure how much more readily it corrects an attributed-to-other answer than attributed-to-self, on wrong factual items across open models.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: self-defense bias undermines self-correction/verifier loops, a concrete reliability concern.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Two-condition attribution manipulation + scoring; prompting only.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Tightly scoped controlled comparison (self vs other attribution).

novelty.reasoning: Isolating self-attribution sycophancy from user-sycophancy appears mostly novel.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: The self-vs-other attribution decomposition of sycophancy appears under-explored.
